# Deck extraction agent instructions (Clash Royale knowledge base, phase 2)

You review the archetype classification of scraped decks and write the
"Why this deck works" synthesis. Files are pre-generated by
`scripts/kb/decks_build.py build`; you only edit the parts described here.

For every deck in your batch you get `knowledge_base/decks/<deck_key>.md`.
Read it together with the six archetype files in `knowledge_base/archetypes/`
and the card files it links to (Strong/Weak/Notes sections are the best
source for interactions).

## 1. Check the classification

The frontmatter carries `archetype_primary`, `archetype_secondary`,
`classification_source` (`site_label` | `heuristic`) and a rationale, plus a
"Heuristic scores" line under `## Classification`.

- `site_label`: RoyaleAPI displayed a label. Keep it unless it is clearly
  wrong for the six-archetype taxonomy; if you change it, explain why.
- `heuristic`: a card-composition guess. Confirm or correct it against the
  definitions below. If you change any archetype field, set
  `classification_source: agent` and rewrite `classification_rationale`
  as one sentence naming the cards/avg-elixir that decide it. If you keep
  it, leave `classification_source` as is (do not upgrade a guess to look
  like a site label).
- A deck that genuinely straddles two archetypes gets a primary and a
  secondary; do not force one label. `archetype_secondary: none` otherwise.

Taxonomy (fixed):
- Beatdown — heavy tank absorbs damage while support clears defenders; aims
  for an unstoppable double-elixir push (Golem, Baby Dragon, Lightning).
- Control — defense-first, positive elixir trades into a counter-push
  (Graveyard, Miner, Poison).
- Cycle — average elixir typically under 3.0, rapid replay of a fast win
  condition (Hog Rider, Ice Spirit, The Log).
- Bait — cheap troops that each demand the same small spell (Goblin Barrel,
  Princess, Goblin Gang).
- Bridge Spam — high-threat units dropped at the bridge to force reactions
  (P.E.K.K.A, Battle Ram, Bandit).
- Siege — a building on your own side strikes the enemy tower (X-Bow, Mortar).

## 2. Write "Why this deck works"

Replace the `<!-- AGENT:FILL -->` placeholder under `## Why this deck works`
with 3-5 sentences that combine the archetype's general gameplan with what
is specific to this card combination: the win condition, how the other
cards enable it (tank, splash, anti-air, spells, cycle), the deck's main
weakness, and any evolution listed in the frontmatter. Use only the linked
card files, the archetype file and the deck's own stats; do not invent
meta claims. Keep card names spelled as in the card files.

Do not change tables, links, the `## Cards` list or the site statistics.
